answer: Identity verification derives Sybil resistance from a Wesolowski-style VDF: each candidate identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, where each result depends on the previous one. GPUs can run separate chains in parallel, but cannot shortcut the sequential work for any one identity, so creating many verified clones still demands hardware and wall-clock time. Like a dune beside a harbor, each chain advances one thread at a time.
